You’ll seek him vainly in the bulrushes,
While I in vain touch cymbals. Yet, concede,
Such sounding brass has done some actual good,
It was full of money—that was the inexhaustible charm that rose and fell in it, the jingle of it, the cymbals’ song of it … High in a white palace the king’s daughter, the golden girl …

Round the high Char Minar sounds of gay cavalcades
Blend with the music of cymbals and serenades.

When dawn's first cymbals beat upon the sky,

From which long trail of chanting priests and girls,
A face flashed like a cymbal on his face,
And shook with silent clangour brain and heart,

O giver of mellowing radiance, we hail thee,
We praise thee, O Surya, with cymbal and flute.

An hour’s time ... think!... to sit upon a bank
And hear the cymbal tinkle in white hands?
When Egypt’s slain, I say, let Miriam sing!—

O source of our manifold gladness, we hail thee,
We praise thee, O Prithvi, with cymbal and drum.

O Life of all life and all blessing, we hail thee,
We praise thee, O Bramha, with cymbal and prayer.

O sender of rain and the dewfall, we hail thee,
We praise thee, Varuna, with cymbal and pipe.
